name: Standardization (z-score) and whitening
where: App B (z-score: (184 − 170) ÷ 7 = 2); Ch 10 (Anomaly detection: Z-score definition, (85 − 40) ÷ 15 = 3, $400 day z = 24). Standardizing features as a preprocessing step and whitening with Σ^(−1/2) are not shown

name: Higher moments (skewness and kurtosis)
where: Not in the book

name: Law of large numbers
where: Ch 6 (Probability > The law of large numbers: 10 flips might give 7 heads, 10,000 flips almost certainly near 5,000; definition; why a 1,000-question test tells you a lot); Ch 6 (Exercise 7 Part 1 code: share of heads should be close to 0.5). name: Central limit theorem
where: Ch 6 (The normal distribution > The bell curve: 'when many small, independent random effects add together, the total tends to follow a bell curve, whatever the individual effects look like'). Not named; sqrt(n) × (mean − μ) ÷ σ → N(0, 1) is not shown

name: Standard error of a mean or proportion
where: Ch 9 (Splitting the data > How sure is the score?: margin 1.96 × sqrt(accuracy × (1 − accuracy) ÷ n), 90% on 1,500 emails gives ±1.5 points, 100 emails ±6; two margins combine by √2; Exercise =1.96*SQRT(B32*(1-B32)/30)); Ch 24 (How precise is a score? Error bars by hand: standard error sqrt(p × (1 − p) ÷ n), 80% on 500 questions 1.79 points); App B (Error bar on an accuracy score). The σ ÷ sqrt(n) form for a mean is not written separately

name: Confidence intervals (normal, t and Wilson) and sample size
where: Ch 24 (How precise is a score? Error bars by hand: 95% interval = about 1.96 standard errors either side, ±3.5 points on 500 questions; Confidence interval definition; Try it =1.96*SQRT(A1*(1-A1)/B1)); Ch 9 (Margin of error definition); Ch 50 (How to read a '% fewer crashes' claim: Poisson 95% range 0.24 to 7.2; Rule of three, 3 ÷ rate = 275 million miles); Ch 57 (four times the participants halves the range). where: Ch 9 (How sure is the score?: significance test logic, p-value and statistical significance definitions, 0.05 cutoff, a 0.8-point gap falls short of about 2 points; paired comparison mentioned); Ch 31 (Worked example: grading two prompts: an exact sign-test p-value, (7 + 1) ÷ 128 ≈ 6%, from 128 equally likely patterns); Ch 54 (Causality: from 'goes with' to 'causes' > The gold standard: randomize). where: Not in the book (App F Generalization bounds describes 'with 95% confidence, the error on new data is at most the training error plus a gap' in words, and Ch 9 names PAC learning, but Markov, Chebyshev, Hoeffding and the union bound are absent)

name: Maximum likelihood estimation (MLE)

where: App F (Classic neural networks and generative-model mathematics > The ELBO, MAP inference and wake-sleep: MAP keeps the single most probable answer, and a prior that weights should be small turns it into ordinary training with L2 regularization; MAP inference definition); Ch 9 (Regularization: L2 penalty worked, without the prior interpretation). ln p(D given θ) + ln p(θ) and the Gaussian and Laplace prior penalties are not shown

where: Not in the book

name: Entropy
where: Ch 6 (Maximum likelihood, entropy and KL divergence: entropy as the average of minus the log of each outcome's probability, fair coin ln 2 ≈ 0.693, exactly 1 bit; the lowest average loss any model can reach; Entropy definition); Ch 21 (Entropy collapse definition, in words). where: Ch 6 (Cross-entropy: how surprised was the model?: loss = −ln(p correct), table; fair coin under a 90/10 model 0.5 × (−ln 0.9) + 0.5 × (−ln 0.1) = 1.204; Exercise 11 grades two models); App B (Cross-entropy, one token and whole text); Ch 8 (Cross-entropy: the loss for categories); Ch 12 (Cross-entropy, for choosing between options)

name: Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence
where: Ch 6 (Maximum likelihood, entropy and KL divergence: KL = cross-entropy minus entropy, 1.204 − 0.693 = 0.511; definition); Ch 20 (The KL leash: KL = sum of p × ln(p ÷ q), worked 0.03 + 0.15 − 0.07 ≈ 0.11; KL penalty). Asymmetry is not discussed and the Gaussian closed form is absent

name: Joint entropy, conditional entropy and the entropy chain rule
where: Not in the book
